ex: We need to have a fresh look at the plan, without blinkers (= we need to consider every aspect of it).
我们应该用新的眼光全面地考虑这个计划。

zh: 目光狭窄的；心胸隘窄的
en: not aware of every aspect of a situation; not willing to accept different ideas about something
ex: a blinkered policy/attitude/approach
褊狭的政策／态度／方法

zh: （委婉语，与 bloody 同义）讨厌，可恶
en: a mild swear word that some people use when they are annoyed, to avoid saying ‘bloody’
ex: Shut the blinking door!
关上那扇该死的门！

zh: a thin pancake that is filled with cheese or fruit, rolled, and then fried or baked
en: a thin pancake that is filled with cheese or fruit, rolled, and then fried or baked
ex: cheese blintzes
奶酪比列兹

zh: 目标标志（雷达屏幕上代表目标的光点）
en: a change in a process or situation, usually when it gets worse for a short time before it gets better; a temporary problem
ex: a temporary blip
暂时的麻烦

en: extreme happiness
ex: married/wedded/domestic bliss
婚后的／家庭的幸福

en: to reach a state of perfect happiness, when you are not aware of anything else
ex: Josh is just blissed out, always smiling.
约什（Josh）高兴极了，总是微笑着。

en: extremely happy; showing happiness
ex: We spent three blissful weeks away from work.
我们无忧无虑地度了三个星期的假。

zh: in a way that makes you extremely happy or that prevents unpleasant things from affecting you
en: extremely happy
ex: blissfully ignorant/unaware
乐得无知／不知情

zh: （皮肤上摩擦或烫等引起的）水疱，疱
（金属、油漆过的木头或其他表面上的）泡，气泡，水泡
en: a swelling (= an area that is larger and rounder than normal) on the surface of the skin that is filled with liquid and is caused, for example, by rubbing or burning
ex: These shoes have given me blisters on my heels.
这些鞋子使我的脚后跟起水泡。

en: a pack in which small goods, such as tablets, are sold, with each individual item in its own separate plastic or foil section on a piece of card

zh: having a surface that is covered with swellings (= round areas filled with air or liquid) and is damaged or split in places
en: with blisters on it
ex: cracked and blistered skin
开裂起疱的皮肤

zh: （描述体育动作）迅速的，劲头十足的
en: (describing actions in sport) done very fast or with great energy
ex: The runners set off at a blistering pace.
赛跑运动员如脱缰野马般起跑了。

zh: 极其，极端，非常（以致使人忌妒）
en: extremely
ex: blisteringly hot
酷热的

en: showing you do not care or are not anxious about what you are doing
ex: He drove with blithe disregard for the rules of the road.
他开车时全然不顾交通法规。

zh: in a happy way; without any worries
en: in a way that shows you do not care or are not anxious about what you are doing
ex: He was blithely unaware of the trouble he'd caused.
他漫不经心，丝毫没有察觉他惹的麻烦。

en: complete
ex: He was a blithering idiot.
他是个十足的傻瓜。

zh: 文学学士（全写为 Bachelor of Letters 或 Bachelor of Literature，大学文科的初级或二级学位）
en: a university degree in an arts subject that may be a first or second degree (the abbreviation for ‘Bachelor of Letters’ or ‘Bachelor of Literature’)

zh: 1940 至 1941 年德国对英国的空袭
集中力量的行动；闪击式行动
en: a sudden attack
ex: Five shops were damaged in a firebomb blitz.
在一次燃烧弹袭击中有五家店铺被烧毁。

en: very drunk
ex: They went out and got blitzed that night.
他们出去当晚被闪电击中。

en: a sudden military attack intended to win a quick victory

zh: 大批侵扰性的事物；大量的负担
en: a snowstorm with very strong winds
ex: blizzard conditions
暴风雪天气

en: to swell (= become bigger or rounder) or make something swell, especially in an unpleasant way
ex: Her features had been bloated by years of drinking.
她酗酒多年，已变得面部浮肿。
